Within 90 days from the base date, have netizens interpreted Country W's consideration of raising taxes on Country X as 'being cornered by Leader A and using the tax increase as a token of trust in exchange for mercy'?

In the 90 days since the base date, has there been repeated arguments on Platform B that "even allies are being stabbed" to prove that "the east rises and the west falls" and just sit back and watch the changes in global trade?

Within 14 days from the base date, has the mainstream public opinion in Platform B fallen into panic due to Leader A’s mass tariff threats and called on the country to make concessions and seek peace on Country Y as soon as possible?

Within 14 days from the base date, if the ally Country G is overweighted, will the main tone of the comment area change to sympathy and support, calling for an alliance with Country G to jointly boycott Country Y?
Within 30 days from the base date, do stock traders generally believe that this round of tariffs will benefit Country Y the domestic manufacturing industry and are bullish on its related sectors?

Within 30 days from the base date, has public opinion confirmed that Leader A has publicly withdrawn the 'letter is an agreement' mechanism and resumed country-by-country negotiations and widely disseminated reports?

Within 60 days from the base date, has the main tone of Country X social media changed from watching movies across the border to worrying that one's own exports will be hit hard and calling for proactive compromise with Country Y?

time.desc: The leader of one party announced in a "mass letter" that he would raise tariffs on multiple trading partners and postpone the effective window for higher tax rates, setting a new cutoff for centralized negotiations.

One party announced the imposition of high tariffs on imported copper and other key industrial products, and signaled that it would use tariff letters as an alternative to traditional negotiation agreements.

One party issued a notice of higher tariffs to a regional group and a major partner and overturned the previous negotiation framework, while warning the other party that retaliation would trigger an overlapping escalation.

Regional groups announced a list of preparations for targeted retaliatory tax increases. At the same time, the sponsors of tax increases significantly softened their public stance to release room for negotiation.
One party reaches a bilateral agreement with its major trading partner to reduce threatened tariffs, including the other party's commitment to expand investment and market opening.

One party used an executive order to advance and expand the cancellation of the tax exemption policy for low-value packages to the world, and at the same time clarified the effective scope of high tariffs on some copper products.

One party's "reciprocal/reciprocal" tariffs were officially implemented at the effective date and covered many countries; on the same day, the domestic court held a key hearing on the legality of extensive tax increase authorization and strong doubts arose.

One party officially announced the implementation of extremely high tariffs on semiconductors and the establishment of exemption and recovery mechanisms for local factory construction. At the same time, it imposed additional punitive tariffs on a large economy, causing the total tax rate to rise significantly.

The highest judicial body agreed to expedite the trial of the extensive tariff authority dispute and arranged a follow-up court schedule, during which the relevant tariffs will continue to be maintained

The two major economies held a new round of economic and trade negotiations to extend the tariff truce arrangement, and included issues such as the disposal of key technology platforms into the overall negotiation package
Trade authorities have launched a formal review process and a public comment period for a regional comprehensive trade agreement, paving the way for possible subsequent renegotiations.

The leader of one party publicly threatened to impose very high tariffs on goods from the other major economy in the future and hinted at expanding export restrictions, making the prospect of a truce worse.
Leaders of sponsoring countries predict 'very high' tariffs on drugs will soon be imposed
An island country in a certain region has become the latest recipient of a tariff letter from the initiating country and has been threatened with a 20% tariff on its exports.

Leaders of the sponsoring countries announced that they would postpone the cutoff for tariff negotiations and threatened to impose high tariffs on more than 20 countries, most of which are located in an export-oriented manufacturing-intensive area.

The head of the government of a long-term ally described the sponsoring country's tariff threat as "deeply regrettable," even though the country has sent representatives to the negotiation venue several times this year.

The leader of the initiating country announced a new tariff on imported goods from a neighboring country and planned to increase the general tariff from 10% to a maximum of 20%, claiming that 'all remaining countries will pay the price'

The leadership of a manufacturing hub partner was surprised by the tariff framework rate announced by the sponsoring country and instructed the negotiation team to continue working hard to lower the rate.

The leader of the initiating country wrote a letter announcing the imposition of high tariffs on a neighboring country's products. The reasons include drug inflow, trade deficit and the country's dairy supply management system.

The Prime Minister's Office of a neighboring country responded that it would convene a cabinet meeting and a meeting of provincial governors to focus on negotiations, and firmly stated that it would defend its workers and companies until the revised cutoff.

The head of state of a neighboring country responded to the tariff letter and was confident that an agreement could be reached before it takes effect, but stressed that his country's sovereignty was never negotiable.

The head of a regional group committee responded that high tariffs will disrupt cross-border supply chains and harm the interests of businesses and consumers on both sides of the Taiwan Strait, but still hopes to persuade the sponsoring country to make concessions.

Leaders of the sponsoring countries issued tariff threats to about twenty-five trading partners within a week, requiring them to sign an agreement that meets the requirements before the cutoff or face punitive tariffs.

Faced with the regional group's preparations for retaliation, the leaders of the sponsoring countries softened their tone significantly in interviews, saying "I don't know how they can retaliate" and saying that the group "is treating us very well now."

The sponsoring country reached a trade agreement with a long-term ally to lower the country's import tariffs from previously threatened levels. The other party promised huge investments and opened the market, while also lowering auto tariffs.

The two major economies confirmed their agreement to extend the tariff truce. The financial chief of the sponsoring country said that the other party's representatives were "a little too hasty" and said that the leaders will make a final decision within two weeks.

The sponsoring country signed an executive order to cancel the tariff exemption for low-value packages in advance and globally. The original applicable threshold was canceled and small-value packages were taxed at the rate of the country of origin.
The sponsoring country announced that it will impose a 50% tariff on some semi-processed metal products and will take effect soon. After the announcement, the metal futures plummeted by nearly 20%.

The federal appeals court held a hearing on the legality of the president's emergency authorization to impose large-scale tariffs and put pressure on government lawyers, just one day before reciprocal tariffs were scheduled to take effect.
The sponsoring country's new round of 'reciprocal' tariffs will officially take effect within a set period, covering dozens of countries, with tax rates ranging from 10% to 40%

A major country in the southern hemisphere was levied an additional 40% tariff due to the trial of the former president, raising the total tax rate to 50%; an energy importing country was threatened with an additional 25% tariff and was given several weeks to respond.
The sponsoring country raised the tariff on imported goods from a neighboring country from 25% to 35% on the grounds of insufficient anti-drug cooperation.

The ambassador and chief negotiator of a neighboring country to the sponsoring country responded that this week's dialogue was professional and constructive, and pointed out that the exemption of goods that comply with existing agreements puts the country in a better position than most countries

The ruling party announced the implementation of a package of punitive tariffs on many countries, covering steel, aluminum, automobiles, agricultural products, etc., ranging from poor small countries to wealthy partners.
A central bank keeps its benchmark interest rate unchanged due to economic uncertainty caused by tariffs

For the first time, the foreign affairs department of an energy-importing country has publicly criticized the sponsoring country's tariff threat as "unfair and unreasonable" and countered that the other country is still trading with the conflicting party.

The initiating country formally imposed an additional 2.5% tariff on an energy importing country, raising the total tax rate to 50%. The country responded by calling the move 'unfair, unreasonable, and without justifiable reasons.'

The authorities of a technology-producing area submitted formal opinions to the sponsoring country on semiconductor tariffs and sought exemptions, warning that tax increases would increase business costs and reduce investment willingness.

The 20% tariff imposed by the sponsoring country on goods from a certain technological origin has officially come into effect, affecting the export of machine tools, plastic products and agricultural products.
Many regional central banks unexpectedly cut interest rates to defend against the impact of the trade war, and a trend of regional monetary easing is taking shape.

For the first time, a head of state from a neighboring country publicly announced that he is studying to impose additional tariffs on imported goods that have not signed a free trade agreement to cope with the pressure of the trade war.

During a meeting with officials from a regional group, the leader of the sponsoring country called on the group to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the two main buyers of oil from the conflict parties to put pressure on ending a certain conflict.
The president must decide whether to implement or delay a law requiring a short-form video app to separate from its foreign parent company

The leaders of the sponsoring countries announced that they plan to use tariff revenue to provide cash assistance to distressed farmers, saying that the assistance will continue until the tariffs begin to have benefits, and the plan must be approved by the legislative body
In soybean purchase negotiations, rival economies have made it clear that they will not give in and blame the sponsoring country's tariff policies for the plight of their own soybean farmers.

The judicial director of the sponsoring country issued a formal notice to an app store operator, requesting the removal of a crowdsourcing app that reminded users to avoid immigration law enforcement. The platform subsequently removed it due to security risks.
